newsitem.title: CANADA: Hibernia partners choose oil tanker manager.
newsitem.headline: Hibernia partners choose oil tanker manager.

text.p: Hibernia oil project partners Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp and Murphy Oil Corp said on Thursday that St. John's, Newfoundland-based Canship Ugland Ltd would shuttle tanker operations for the project.
The partners said the agreement provided for Canship Ugland to operate the vessel on behalf of the three companies for an initial period of five years.
The group, which includes the Canadian divisions of Mobil, Murphy and Chevron, also said the vessel would be named the Motor Tanker (MIT) Kometik.

The tanker news coincided with the Hibernia owners' announcement that they would locate a C$100-million transshipment terminal on Newfoundland's Avalon Peninsula at Whiffin Head, about five km from North Atlantic Refining Ltd 's Come By Chance refinery.
Under the deal, Canship Ugland would be responsible for supplying the tanker crew, provisions and stores, repair and maintenance, management and administration.
Costs were anticipated to be about C$8 million a year, the partners said.
Canship Ugland is an affiliate of Penney Ugland Ltd, which is a joint venture between Canship of the St. John's-based Pennecon group of companies and the J J Ugland Group of Grimstad, Norway.

The partners said the Kometik, jointly owned by Mobil Oil Canada Properties, Chevron Canada Resources and Murphy Atlantic Offshore Oil Company, was being constructed by Samsung Heavy Industries in Korea and was expected to be completed in August 1997.
The Kometik would be Canadian flagged and crewed with Canadian personnel generating job opportunities for 45-50 Canadians, theyt said.

Partners in Hibernia are Petro-Canada Hibernia Partnership with 25 percent, Mobil unit Mobil Oil Canada Ltd with 33.125 percent, Chevron Corp unit Chevron Canada Resources with 26.875 percent, Murphy Oil Corp's Murphy Atlantic Offshore Oil Co Ltd with 6.5 percent and the government of Canada's Canada Hibernia Holding Corp with 8.5 percent.
